answer: Unrepeatable challenge assay. Each identity must solve a fresh physical challenge: grow a quartz resonator to a specified frequency tolerance, then log its drift curve into a sealed vault. The curve is checked against the resonator's own measured noise floor, so copied curves fail. Registration also requires a timber sample whose grain pattern is imaged once and retired. An attacker pays one lab-grown crystal and one destroyed sample per identity, plus hours of per-unit calibration that cannot be batched or resold.
